toegepas.voor: roep hard na iemand ver weg
toegepas.na: roep hard na iemand wat ver weg is
toegepas.rede_vinder: The bare 'iemand ver weg' is elliptical and reads like a translation; a relative clause is the natural Afrikaans form.
toegepas.fout: 'iemand ver weg' is an elliptical, slightly English-shaped phrase
toegepas.rede_keurder: The relative clause is the natural Afrikaans form and says exactly the same thing.

toegepas.voor: Die punt wat jy verder afdruk, laat die liniaal wyer swaai en harder klink
toegepas.na: As jy die punt verder afdruk, swaai die liniaal wyer en klink dit harder
toegepas.rede_vinder: It is the pressing, not the point, that makes the ruler swing wider; a conditional clause says this plainly and reads naturally.
toegepas.fout: Wooden construction that makes the point, rather than the pressing, the cause
toegepas.rede_keurder: The conditional reads naturally, keeps the same cause and effect, and 'swaai wyer' and 'harder' stay on volume as the protected rule requires.

toegepas.voor: en net jou afdruk het verander
toegepas.na: en net hoe ver jy die punt afdruk, het verander
toegepas.rede_vinder: As a noun 'afdruk' means a print or imprint in Afrikaans, not the act of pressing down; the verb phrase says what is meant.
toegepas.fout: The noun 'afdruk' means a print or imprint, not the act of pressing down
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'hoe ver jy die punt afdruk' names exactly the variable the paragraph changed, so nothing is added and the wrong noun is gone.

toegepas.blok: Die liniaal wys dat hulle twee dinge is
toegepas.rede_vinder: The drum itself is not loud and low, its sound is; 'klink' matches the rest of the lesson and avoids the flat 'is hard' right after 'hard geslaan'.
toegepas.fout: 'is hard' says the drum itself is loud (and can be read as physically hard) and echoes 'hard geslaan' just before
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'klink' puts the loudness and pitch on the sound, matches 'klink hoog maar sag' in the sentence before, and leaves the protected hard/laag pairing intact.

na_skrywer.voor: Die vorige toets het gewys dat 'n ander afdruk die noot nie verander nie
na_skrywer.na: Die vorige toets het gewys dat die noot dieselfde bly, hoe ver jy die punt ook al afdruk
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: The noun 'afdruk' means an imprint, so 'n ander afdruk' reads as 'a different print'; the verb form keeps the meaning that pressing further leaves the note unchanged.
na_skrywer.fout: The noun 'afdruk' means a print or imprint, not the act of pressing down
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The fault is real, but 'hoe ver ... ook al' widens what the test showed (two press depths) into a claim about any depth, so the claim moves and the writer must fix the noun another way.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.blok: Die liniaal wys dat hulle twee dinge is
na_skrywer.voor: Jy het pas gehoor dat 'n ander afdruk die noot nie verander nie
na_skrywer.na: Jy het pas gehoor dat die noot dieselfde bly, hoe ver jy die punt ook al afdruk
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: Same noun 'afdruk' problem as in the previous block; kept parallel with that sentence.
na_skrywer.fout: The noun 'afdruk' means a print or imprint, not the act of pressing down
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: Same as change 4: the noun needs fixing, but the proposed 'hoe ver ... ook al' broadens the claim beyond what was heard, so it goes to the writer.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.blok: Wat 'n klank hoër maak / Die liniaal wys dat hulle twee dinge is
vlae.rede: If the reviewer keeps only one of the two 'afdruk' sentence changes, the two blocks will word the same point differently; they should be decided together. The 'hoe ver ... ook al' wording is slightly wider than 'a different press', so check it keeps the meaning.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: en lyk net soos 'n vae band
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The ruler's tip does not become a band, it looks like one; lyk soos says what the sentence means.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'word net 'n vae band' is accepted figurative Afrikaans, and the proposal turns 'net' (only) into 'net soos' (just like), shifting the sense.
